subject: Follow-up: Latency & throughput A/B test plan + preliminary results
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@globex.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@globex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T16:20:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Latency & throughput A/B test plan + preliminary results

Hi Sam & Alicia,

Thanks again for taking the call today — really appreciated the deep dive on your realtime inference needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: validate ~50 concurrent sessions of short-chat traffic (avg 80 tokens/request) with p95 latency < 120ms and p99 < 300ms for the production prompt-set.
- What we ran on the call: quick 1k-step microbench comparing Redwood Dedicated configuration (A100s, q4/8 quant) vs Hyperscaler X managed inference (vCPU-backed variant) — results looked promising but noisy.

Next steps we discussed:
1) Run a controlled A/B test across your representative prompt set (we'll run identical prompts, same token distribution).
2) Capture p50/p95/p99, tail jitter, and tokens/sec. Also collect throughput under batch sizes 1, 4, 8.
3) Share raw CSV + summary PDF and schedule a 30-min sync to review results and decide on Dedicated sizing.

I've looped in Rishi and Vivek to support the A/B test and to provide config snippets and runbooks. We can run an initial 10k-request run Wednesday if that works for you.

Attachments: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks_summary.pdf (summary), raw_abtest_tokens_latency.csv (raw).

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@globex.com>
Date: 2026-02-13T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Latency & throughput A/B test plan + preliminary results

Marissa,

Appreciate the recap. Wednesday works for an initial run — can you confirm the exact time (we're PST). A couple clarifying items before we kick off:

- For p95/p99, are you reporting server-side service time or end-to-end (including network hops)? We want server-side numbers for apples-to-apples with our internal agent.
- Can you include tokens/sec at the model level and at the QPS level (tokens/sec per GPU and overall tokens/sec observed)?
- Any chance to add a 95th percentile memory footprint or KV-cache usage for the prompts with long histories?

Also, is there any limitation on payload size for the prompt history? Our sessions often have ~1.2k tokens history.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Patel
Senior Platform Engineer, Globex Corp
sam.patel@globex.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@globex.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Latency & throughput A/B test plan + preliminary results

Hi Sam — quick answers inline:

- We report server-side inference latency (server processing only) by default in the summary PDF. For E2E you can add client-side timing; we can include both in the CSV.
- We'll include tokens/sec at the model (per-GPU) level and observed tokens/sec at the aggregate QPS. The CSV has per-request timestamps so you can compute both; summary shows tokens/sec per GPU at median and p95.
- Memory/KV-cache: we'll capture peak GPU memory and KV-cache size sampled every 100 requests. For very long histories (1.2k tokens) we'll test with both full history and truncated-prefix caching to show tradeoffs.
- Payload limits: Redwood supports ~8k token contexts on the config we're using. For the test we'll run with your 1.2k history to be realistic.

Proposed schedule:
- Wed 2026-02-18 10:00 PST: 10k requests (steady ramp) A/B test (Redwood vs Hyperscaler X).
- Wed 2026-02-18 11:00 PST: 30-min sync to review results.

We'll push the run results to the Drive link and attach the CSV + summary in the follow-up email.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@globex.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@globex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-16T14:40:00-08:00
Subject: Preliminary A/B micro-bench summary (attached)

Hi team —

We ran a focused micro-benchmark (3k requests) using your representative prompt set to validate the harness before Wed's larger run. Attaching a short summary PDF and raw CSV. Highlights below:

- Redwood (Dedicated - A100 q4/8, batch=1):
  - p50: 42ms, p95: 98ms, p99: 210ms
  - tokens/sec (per-GPU median): 12.8k tok/s
  - observed aggregate tokens/sec (single-GPU run): 12.6k tok/s
  - tail jitter during cold start spikes (p99) observed for first ~200 requests.
- Hyperscaler X (managed inference):
  - p50: 85ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 520ms
  - tokens/sec (per-instance): 6.4k tok/s
  - noted higher variance under batching >4

Notes: metrics above are server-side processing time only. We sampled GPU memory/kv-cache for the long-history cases and saw ~7.8GB avg KV footprint for the 1.2k token history on Redwood. Hyperscaler X numbers came from their managed config with similar GPU class but lower optimized kernels for quantized models.

Attaching: redwood_vs_hyperscaler_benchmarks_summary.pdf, raw_abtest_tokens_latency.csv

Let us know if this aligns with what you expect and any extra columns you'd like in the CSV for the full A/B test.

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@globex.com>, Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@globex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Wed A/B run complete — Next steps + proposed analysis

Hi Sam & Alicia —

Thanks for running the A/B test window this morning. Quick notes and proposed analysis plan:

- We completed 10k requests per variant (Redwood vs Hyperscaler X) with your production prompt-set. Raw CSV is attached and live in the Drive link.
- Preliminary aggregated results (server-side):
  - Redwood: p50 45ms, p95 102ms, p99 225ms, aggregate tokens/sec observed 12.1k
  - Hyperscaler X: p50 88ms, p95 235ms, p99 540ms, aggregate tokens/sec observed 6.0k
  - Under batch=4 Redwood tokens/sec per-GPU improves to ~14.5k with p95 still <140ms in our run.
  - Tail: Hyperscaler X showed several 1-2s outliers at p99 likely due to cold container spins; we captured start-up traces in the CSV.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra team (30-45 min) to review raw traces and kernel selection differences (Rishi & Vivek to lead).
2) If you want, we can run an additional pass with pinned warm instances and a replicate of your highest-concurrency window (50 concurrent sessions) to validate p95 SLA at scale.
3) Commercial: based on these numbers we can propose Dedicated sizing and a pricing estimate for committed capacity — happy to draft a mutual action plan.

Please confirm preferred time for the deep-dive (we're available Tue/Thu next week).

Thanks again — attaching raw_abtest_tokens_latency.csv and the summary PDF.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
